data.turoyo: <...> komər bəṯər məd mawfaqle i kačke azze li nvinayḏe l Aloho xləqle zʕuro ʕam i aṯto. <...>
data.translation: <...> Nachdem er das Mädchen (aus dem Steinhaufen) herausgeholt hatte, ging er in sein Bett, da schuf Gott ein Kind bei seiner Frau. <...>

rationale: Thin Preterit cell; divine creator, child object and maternal association.

data.turoyo: <...> Omər: "Zox tayli ʕafro mann arbaʕ qərnawoṯo d briṯo d xulqina Oḏəm." <...>
data.translation: <...> "Geh, hole mir Staub von den vier Enden der Welt, damit wir Adam erschaffen." <...>

rationale: Thin Infectum cell; first-person plural purpose clause contrasted with realized creation.

data.turoyo: <...> Mšiḥo, u šubḥayḏe, mamṭele ʕafro w xləqle Oḏəm, hawi xwoṯe. <...>
data.translation: <...> Inzwischen aber holte Christus, ihm sei Ehre, Staub und schuf den Adam; so dass er wurde wie er. <...>

rationale: Independent realized creation of Adam, complementary to the purpose construction.

data.turoyo: <...> Aloho xləqle sawko lu ənsan, lu barnošo, me kul šəkəl daʔ ʔalwan.
data.translation: <...> Gott hat dem Menschen das Haar in allen Arten von Farben geschaffen.

rationale: Explicit l-marked beneficiary beside zero-marked hair object; brings Preterit to five.

summary: Restore š in both occurrences of šubḥo
rationale: The supplied 74/4 corpus has Ele šəbḥo l aloho, šəbḥo lu xaloqo, twice with initial š, whereas the quotation has s twice. Correct the consonant and retain the entry’s vowel u and clitic normalization.

summary: All active uses retain I.1 creation. Human/child, hair and universe objects differ in participant type, not verbal meaning.
L-marked divine agent can precede or follow the verb; created objects are zero-marked or indexed by feminine -o- (74/4,115/189). Beneficiary l-NPs are distinct from agents in84/14,45.
PrS55/2 contrasts planned first-person plural creation in a purpose clause with realized third-person singular creation by Christ.

The inherited Detransitive Preterit xliq aʕma zʕuro has the boy as patient subject and a mother-associated ʕam phrase. The narrative places it with pregnancy; the edition's got-a-boy rendering does not alone distinguish conception from birth.
Existing unlabelled examples are counted under implicit sense1. Detransitive1 is inherited through its examples although no separate gloss list is printed.
64/243: does xliq aʕma zʕuro denote conception here, as distinct from the later birth? Preserve the existing quotation pending edition/context review.
Supply the missing Detransitive sense1 gloss, distinguishing the birth/conception frame from generic being created if appropriate.
